items.entity: cantilever design domain (length L x height H x width W)
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 gives no dimensions. It says only that the problem is 'the same as the numerical examples considered in [64]' (not provided) and that the domain is shown in Fig. 3 (left), which is not available. The actual size matters, not just the proportions, because the filter radius is given in metres (r = 0.1 m) and the mass bound may be an absolute value.
readings: 3 m x 1 m x 1 m (3:1:1; matches 30x10x10 cube elements of 0.1 m)
1.5 m x 0.5 m x 0.5 m (3:1:1; 30x10x10 cube elements of 0.05 m)
2 m x 1.5 m x 1 m (matches 20x15x10 cube elements of 0.1 m)
2 m x 1 m x 1 m (2:1:1; elements cannot be cubes with 3000 elements)
6 m x 1 m x 0.5 m (thin beam; 60x10x5 cube elements of 0.1 m)

items.entity: element grid nx x ny x nz for the 3 000 / 24 000 / 192 000 design-variable meshes
items.description: The text gives only the total number of design variables (one per element, per Sec. 2) and says 'structured mesh with uniform hexahedral first-order finite elements'. Each mesh has 8 times as many elements as the last, which suggests the element size is halved in every direction. However, the 3 000-element starting grid and the element shape (cube or not) are not stated. It is also not said which of the three meshes produced the optimal design in Fig. 3 (right).

The text never describes the support for this example. The word 'cantilever' implies that one end is fixed, but which face, and whether all or part of it is supported, is shown only in Fig. 3 (left) or in [64].
readings: entire end face x = 0 (0<=y<=W, 0<=z<=H)
only the top and bottom edges (lines) of the end face x = 0
central patch of the end face x = 0 (e.g. middle 50% of the height, full width)

items.entity: constrained displacement components on the supported face
items.description: The blade example (Sec. 6.1.2) says 'fixed boundary condition', but the cantilever text never says which displacement components are held. Only the word 'cantilever' suggests a full clamp.
readings: all three translations fixed (fully clamped)
only the displacement normal to the face (along the beam axis) fixed, plus the minimum constraints needed to stop rigid-body motion

items.entity: external load on the cantilever (free end)
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 does not mention a load at all. Where it acts is defined only in Fig. 3 (left) or [64].
readings: centre of the free-end face (x = L, y = W/2, z = H/2)
middle of the bottom edge of the free-end face (x = L, y = W/2, z = 0)
middle of the top edge of the free-end face (x = L, y = W/2, z = H)

items.entity: how the free-end load is spread
items.description: The text does not say whether the load is a single point force, a line load across the width, or a pressure over an area (it appears only in Fig. 3 left).
readings: single concentrated force at one node
line load spread evenly across the full width W at the chosen height
uniform traction over the whole free-end face
traction over a small patch (e.g. 2x2 elements) around the load point

items.description: The direction is not given in the text. With a single load, the sign (up or down) does not change the compliance. Whether the load acts along the height or along the width does matter, unless the cross-section is square and the load is centred.
readings: across the beam, along its height (e.g. -z, 'downward')
across the beam, along its width (e.g. -y)

items.description: No load value is given. It cannot be worked back from the reported compliances (about 13.2 to 13.6) because Young's modulus and the domain size are also uncertain.
readings: 1 N (unit load)
1 kN
10 N (same as the blade example in Sec. 6.1.2)

items.entity: upper bound of 0.5 on the mass constraint
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 says 'The upper bound for the mass constraint is 0.5'. In Eq. (1), the bound v_u is an absolute total volume. The example calls it a mass bound but gives no material density, and the domain volume is unknown. So it is unclear whether 0.5 is a fraction of the domain or an absolute amount.
readings: volume fraction 0.5 of the design-domain volume
absolute material volume v_u = 0.5 m^3, i.e. a fraction of 0.5/V_domain (about 0.167 for a 3 m^3 domain, 0.25 for a 2 m^3 domain)

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 of the solid
items.description: The value is printed as '2.0 x 10^{1}1 N/m^2', so the exponent is garbled.
readings: 2.0e11 N/m^2 (steel; fits with Poisson's ratio 0.29)
2.0e1 = 20 N/m^2 (the printed text read literally)

items.entity: minimum stiffness for void elements in SIMP
items.description: Eq. (4), E = rho^s E0 with 0 <= mu <= 1, gives zero stiffness to void elements. No minimum stiffness (E_min) or minimum density (rho_min) is stated, yet one is needed to keep the stiffness matrix solvable with the conjugate-gradient solver and multigrid preconditioner.
readings: E_min = 0 (Eq. (4) as written; rely on the filter to keep rho > 0)
modified SIMP: E = E_min + rho^3 (E0 - E_min) with E_min = 1e-9 E0
lower bound rho_min = 1e-3 on the densities (E_min = 1e-9 E0 with s = 3)

items.entity: Helmholtz filter radius measured in elements
items.description: r = 0.1 m (the parameter in Eq. (3)) is given in metres. Because the domain size and grid are unknown (see above), the radius in element lengths cannot be determined. If the engineer's solver uses a standard cone (density) filter instead, the equivalent radius is R = 2*sqrt(3)*r, about 0.35 m.
readings: element size 0.1 m on the 3 000-element mesh -> r = 1, 2, 4 elements on the three meshes
element size 0.2 m -> r = 0.5, 1, 2 elements
element size 0.05 m -> r = 2, 4, 8 elements

items.entity: Helmholtz filter boundary conditions and discretization
items.description: Eq. (3) is given without boundary conditions. The text also does not say whether the filtered density rho is stored at nodes or per element. Both choices affect the design near the supports, the load and the free surfaces.
readings: zero-flux (homogeneous Neumann) condition on the whole boundary (standard Lazarov-Sigmund form)
zero-flux condition with the domain padded or extended to reduce boundary effects
rho = 0 fixed (Dirichlet) on the free boundaries

items.description: The IPOPT starting point is never given. The problem has more than one local optimum: the text notes that the incremental-SVD run with 3 000 variables 'converges to a different local minimum'. So the starting design can change the final layout.
readings: uniform mu0 = 0.5 (equal to the volume bound)
uniform mu0 = 1.0 (fully solid)
uniform mu0 just below the bound (e.g. 0.49, strictly inside the feasible region)

items.entity: IPOPT options other than the convergence tolerance
items.description: Only 'IPOPT ... with convergence threshold of 10^-6' is given. The paper describes only gradients, so IPOPT presumably used a quasi-Newton Hessian approximation, but this is not stated. Also unstated are the memory size, the barrier-parameter strategy, scaling and the iteration limit. These settings affect the path the optimizer takes and which local optimum it reaches; the IPOPT iteration counts in Tables 1 to 3 vary widely.
readings: hessian_approximation = limited-memory (L-BFGS, default memory 6), all other options default
limited-memory with a larger memory (e.g. 20) and the adaptive barrier strategy (mu_strategy = adaptive)
exact Hessian supplied

items.entity: regions fixed as solid or void (non-design)
items.description: No such regions are mentioned. Fig. 3 (left) or [64] could include solid pads at the load or the support.
readings: no fixed regions (the whole box can be designed)
a solid, non-design pad around the load point
a solid, non-design layer next to the clamped face

items.entity: number of cantilever set-ups shown in Fig. 3
items.description: Sec. 6.1.1 says 'The design domains and optimal designs for two problems are shown in Figure 3'. The caption, however, shows only one domain and one optimal design, both for the cantilever.
readings: a single cantilever set-up ('two problems' means the cantilever and the blade in Sec. 6.1)
two cantilever versions from [64] (e.g. different load cases), of which only one is shown or described

items.entity: full model vs. symmetric half model
items.description: The text does not say whether the 3 000 / 24 000 / 192 000 design variables cover the whole beam or a symmetric half, which is a common simplification for symmetric 3-D cantilevers. A half model would double the effective resolution and need symmetry boundary conditions.
readings: full domain with the stated element counts
half domain (symmetry plane at mid-width, displacement normal to that plane fixed), equal to 6 000 / 48 000 / 384 000 elements for the whole beam
